messages:
jen: DeployBot flagged a regression in eu-west1 canary (latency spike, ~4x p50). Can we get expedited decision to either pin the previous image or rollback the release? @aaron_oncall @sam

sam: seeing the alert, digging into traces now. ETA 5m. Do we have an easy pin command?

jen: yes -- we can pin the fleet to `redwood/serve:2026.03.18` which was healthy. If we rollback it'll be a staged cutover. Prefer pin if it's a small perf regression tied to kernel flags.

maria: quick note: release notes already published for the version, need to update changelog if we revert. Who will own the release-note edit?

aaron_oncall: I'm on call, prioritizing rollback decision. Sam, any signal from traces?

sam: traces show a spike in tokenization latency on a small subset of hosts after the latest kernel bump. Not seeing model regressions. Repro locally with the same kernel image. My vote: pin to previous image in eu-west1, then run a canary check for 30m.

deploybot: Automated check: canary-failures=3, p50-ms=420 -> threshold-exceeded. Suggested action: `pin` or `rollback`. Use `/deploy approve` to confirm fast action.

jen: agree with pin. If we pin, ops will route new requests to pinned pool while we investigate kernel. Can someone run the pin and post command?

aaron_oncall: issuing pin now:
`/deploy pin --region eu-west1 --image redwood/serve:2026.03.18 --reason "post-release kernel perf regression"`

releasebot: Pin request accepted. Starting rolling pin in eu-west1. Expected completion ~4 minutes. Notifying on-call and release owners.

sam: Thanks. After pin completes, can we run a dry-run load test against the pinned group and confirm p50 back to baseline? I'll queue a 5m smoke with 5qps.

opsbot: Rollout complete: 12/12 hosts pinned. Health checks: passing. Telemetry shows p50 back to baseline within 90s.

maria: I'll patch the release notes: add a short "Reverted platform kernel bump in eu-west1 due to latency regression; investigating" line and bump the changelog timestamp. Pushing commit to docs repo now.

jen: excellent. No rollback required then. Sam, please follow up with kernel owners and file an infra ticket. Aaron, thanks for quick pin. :thumbsup:

aaron_oncall: Filed INFRA-4271 with traces and repro steps. Marking this thread resolved unless new alerts come in.

jen: closing the expedited approval. Leaving the canary monitoring rule at higher sensitivity for 24h.

sam: will monitor for 2h and report back. If anything else, I'll reopen.
